issues.issue: The waterfall pays the Certificate Insurer its Premium Distribution Amount and Aggregate Certificate Insurer Reimbursement Amount ahead of Mezzanine interest and principal, and pays Unpaid Realized Loss Amounts on the Class 1-A-3, 2-A-3 and 4-A-2 Certificates only 'to the extent not covered by the Certificate Insurance Policy,' which requires reading the priorities against the Policy and Endorsement No. 1 and the deemed-balance proviso in the definition of Certificate Principal Balance. Whether insured holders or the insurer are entitled to a given dollar cannot be determined from this section alone.

Within each senior group, Applied Realized Loss Amounts are written down first against the insured class (Class 1-A-3, Class 2-A-3 and Class 4-A-2) before the uninsured classes, while the definition of Certificate Principal Balance deems the insured classes' balances not reduced by insurer payments 'solely' for premium and subrogation purposes. Whether a written-down insured certificate retains a claim, and against whom, only appears from reading the two together.

Subsequent Recoveries are allocated here to increase the Class Principal Balances of the Class 1-A-3, Class 2-A-3 and Class 4-A-2 Certificates, while the definition of Certificate Principal Balance provides that Subsequent Recoveries payable to those classes 'shall be payable to the Certificate Insurer' to the extent the loss was paid under the Policy. The two directions cover the same money.

The opening parenthetical directs that the principal and interest figures 'be expressed as a dollar amount per one thousand' (and is never closed), while the closing sentence of the same subsection directs that the same figures be expressed 'as a dollar amount per single Certificate of the relevant Class.' The two instructions for items (i) and (ii) contradict each other.

The Trust Administrator's responsibility 'is limited to the availability, timeliness and the accuracy of the information provided by each Servicer,' which as written makes it responsible for exactly what it evidently means to disclaim. The sentence reverses the intended limitation.

The Master Servicer must use its 'reasonable best efforts' to make a Servicer correct information, a compound standard the Agreement does not define. What that requires when a Servicer refuses is unstated.

The Supplemental Interest Trust is established for the benefit of the holders of the Senior and Mezzanine Certificates, yet Section 2.01(f) excludes the Group 3 Certificates from the Cap Contract arrangement and Sections 3.07(i) and (j) give the Class C Certificates ownership of the Cap Accounts held for that trust. Who benefits from the supplemental trust is stated differently in each place.

The priorities in this subsection are numbered (11) through (18) and then '(9) ninth,' although they are described as 'first' through 'ninth' in a self-contained sequence. The numbering does not correspond to the order or to the cross-references made to it elsewhere.

Distributions run to 'the Mezzanine Cap Contract Scheduled Termination Date,' a term the Agreement does not define; the defined date is the 'Mezzanine Cap Contract Termination Date.' The end of the distribution period is fixed by an undefined term.

The MTA fallback uses 'the Reserve Interest Rate,' a term defined only inside Section 4.10 by reference to one-month U.S. dollar LIBOR quotations, which is not a substitute for a twelve-month Treasury average. Importing that rate into the MTA determination produces a rate of a different character.

The margin adjustment is 'the difference between MTA for the final three years it was in effect and the average of the most recent three years for the replacement index,' comparing an unaveraged index figure with an average. The computation cannot be performed as literally written.

COFI is to be taken from FHLB San Francisco statistics 'as most recently available generally as of a day specified in the related note,' although the Certificates are not notes and no such day is specified anywhere. The determination date for the index is left unfixed.

The COFI fallback substitutes 'the Reserve Interest Rate,' which Section 4.10 defines by reference to one-month U.S. dollar interbank lending quotations rather than to any cost-of-funds measure. The substitute index is of a different kind from the one it replaces.

Certificates are issuable 'in the minimum denominations, integral multiples in excess thereof ... and aggregate denominations per Class set forth in the Preliminary Statement,' but the Preliminary Statement sets out class designations, rates and balances and states no minimum denominations. The authorized denominations must be found somewhere other than where this section sends the reader.

This section makes countersignature by the Trust Administrator 'conclusive evidence, and the only evidence,' that a Certificate was duly executed, while Section 11.10 speaks of the Certificates 'upon due authentication thereof by the Trustee.' Which act validates a Certificate is stated differently in the two places.

For an ERISA-Restricted Certificate that is neither a Private nor a Residual Certificate the required representation is 'deemed to have been made ... by the transferee's ... acceptance,' yet the final sentence makes any transfer to or on behalf of a Plan 'void and of no effect.' A deemed representation and an automatic voiding cannot both govern the same transfer.
